newsitem.title: USA: Dollar exceeds 120 yen, then falls on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Dollar exceeds 120 yen, then falls on profit-taking.

text.p: The dollar fell against the yen Friday after conflicting signals from Japanese officials prompted profit-taking, toppling the dollar from its highest level in nearly four years.

The dollar earlier rose above 120 yen in Tokyo after Japanese officials said the falling stock market and weak yen would not stall Japan's economy. But the dollar later dropped and remained lower in New York trading amid talk that the Bank of Japan had sold dollars for yen.

Additional remarks by Japanese officials later took steam out of the U.S. currency. An official at the Japanese finance ministry said an excessively weak yen was not welcome while Japan's chief government spokesman expressed confidence that the yen would not weaken past 120 per dollar.

"Like excessive appreciation ... an excessive depreciaton of the yen is not welcome," the finance official told reporters in Tokyo. But the official declined to say at what level the yen would be considered excessively weak.
The dollar fell to 118.85 yen late in New York from 119.31 late on Thursday.
The dollar fell to 1.6283 German marks from 1.6325 marks on Thursday, when it touched a fresh 31-month high at 1.6455 but later fell back.
A drop in stock and bond prices on Wall Street weighed on the dollar during U.S. trading.

The 30-year Treasury fell more than half a point Friday before recovering somewhat to end off 12/32, or $3.75 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.89 percent from 6.86 on Thursday. Bond prices and yields move in the opposite direction.

"People were taken aback by the very sharp weakness in bonds," said Alfonso Alejo, a vice president at Sakura Bank Ltd. The attack on bonds spilled over and "the dollar came under some pressure," he said.
But the dollar got a modest boost late in the session after the Dow Jones industrial average recouped some of its earlier loss of 95 points. Stocks ended off 59.27 points at 6,696.48.
"They sold it (the dollar) down, now the Dow has sort of recovered a little bit, so people are buying it back," said Sanwa's Yu. "There is no rhyme or reason right now for the market."
The dollar fell to 1.4060 Swiss francs from 1.4160 Thursday. It rose to Canadian $1.3495 from C$1.3449.
The British pound fell to $1.6315 from $1.6320.
